reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected GAAP exhibit rows shows revenue growth concentrated in the financial technology solutions component, with subscription services also higher and hardware and professional services lower. Gross profit rose while costs of revenue also rose, and operating expenses increased by a similar order, so GAAP operating income improved only marginally relative to the revenue and gross profit movement. The larger step in GAAP net income is not explained by operations alone: the warrant fair value line moved from a loss to a gain, and the income tax line moved from a benefit to an expense, which partly offsets the pretax improvement. The tax movement is an increase in tax expense, not a smaller tax drag. Company-reported gross payment volume rose on its own operating basis and is not revenue. All of this is displayed-value arithmetic on selected rows, not a causal attribution, not a year-over-year comparison, and not a comparison against guidance or consensus; no non-GAAP measures, guidance, or segment-level drivers are in the selected extract. The thesis remains active with unchanged conviction because the selected evidence is consistent with continued sequential growth and modest GAAP operating leverage, but it does not establish durability, mix-driven margin mechanics, or any valuation conclusion. Evidence that would change the view: full-filing segment and cost detail, non-GAAP reconciliations, guidance versus realized results, year-over-year comparatives, and disclosure on the warrant remeasurement and tax drivers.
